title: Frontend security that affects everyday code
outcome: Separate trusted markup, outside text, browser storage, and server authorization.
useCase: Rich tooltips, support descriptions, and product analytics.
benefits: Makes common trust boundaries visible in everyday UI work.
drawbacks: Rich content and third-party SDKs require ongoing policy maintenance.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: If the browser receives it, the user can inspect it.

trace.title: Outside data
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Outside text is data. Rendering it as HTML can turn it into executable behavior.

Vue’s ordinary interpolation escapes text; v-html crosses a different boundary. If rich HTML is required, use a maintained sanitizer with an explicit policy and keep it updated.

Browser storage is available to code running in the origin. It is not a secret vault.

A script injection can read accessible tokens and drafts. Cookie settings, CSRF protection, Content Security Policy, and server access checks address different risks.

Never send a field to the browser just because it is hidden visually. Client props, network payloads, source maps, logs, and analytics can all reveal information.

Select permitted data on the server and keep telemetry deliberately small.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Input arrives → validate shape → decide text versus rich content → render through the right boundary → enforce server permissions for actions. Audit the payload and telemetry, not just pixels.

Test a title containing markup-looking text. It should appear as text.

Test a direct unauthorized request without using the UI. These are different checks.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A hidden field in a client payload is still present. A client filter is not a tenant boundary.

Escaping output does not validate a destination URL or authorize a mutation.
